abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) diagrams are widely used to communicate nucleic acid secondary structure, yet the path from a sequence and pairing model to an editable publication figure often requires either specialized software or substantial cleanup in a general-purpose graphics editor. AptaRender (v2.3.1, available at https://yjhe99.github.io/aptarender/) is a browser-based editor that converts a set of user-supplied DNA or RNA sequences and their dot-bracket structures into an interactive 2D drawing. The software separates structure specification from visual composition: it does not predict folding, but provides direct control over the layout, nucleotide styling, base pair styling, numbering and export. AptaRender supports simultaneously working with multiple sequences, customized per-nucleotide sizing and coloring with customized styles, manual branching and motif repositioning, constrained rotation of helices around loop rings, and visualization of a user defined hybridization region between two strands. Drawings are exported as editable SVG or high-resolution PNG. The application is implemented as a single dependency-free HTML file that runs entirely in the browser and stores working state locally. This design makes the tool easy to distribute and suitable for rapid preparation of figures for manuscripts, presentations, and exploratory communication. AptaRender complements prediction and template-based visualization software by concentrating on lightweight, local, art directed figure construction. Across eight test cases, AptaRender reliably generated accurate, information-rich 2D nucleic acid structures and exported them in PNG and SVG formats, although specialized annotations and additional symbols required external editing.
